title: The Samadhiraja Sutra — the Sanskrit text
textType: Mahayana sutra in prose and verse
attributionNote: One of the nine dharmaparyāyas of the Nepalese Buddhist canon, transmitted without an author and closely related to the Samādhirāja verses quoted at length by Śāntideva's Śikṣāsamuccaya. GRETIL's e-text follows P. L. Vaidya's edition (Darbhanga 1961, Buddhist Sanskrit Texts 2) and was input by the Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon Input Project.
description: The Samādhirājasūtra is the sutra of the samādhi that the Buddhas of the past, present and future enter, and of the vision of all phenomena as like the moon in water, like a mirage, like a dream: it teaches that the dharmas taught in the assemblies of the Buddha are to be found in the emptiness of all things, that the great compassion of a Bodhisattva is the entrance to this samādhi, and that a verse of it recited with faith outweighs immeasurable offerings. Its thirty-nine chapters of prose and verse, with the long verse sequences in which the Buddha answers Candraprabha, are among the deepest meditative sutras of the Mahayana.
historicalContext: The sutra was quoted by the Madhyamaka and the Yogācāra alike, cited by Śāntideva and by the compilers of the Tibetan canon, and preserved in Sanskrit in Nepalese manuscripts whose publication by Vaidya made it available in the original.
availabilityNote: Complete as GRETIL publishes it: all thirty-nine chapters with their prose and verse, 2,063 passages, streamed from GRETIL at read time, one chapter at a time. The file prints the title and the first chapter's heading above the opening lines and the reader drops them from the text. This is the original Sanskrit, not a translation.
